transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble at work lately. I do camera work and video editing, and... well, it finally kind of scared me into coming in. 

I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes. Things I definitely know better than to make. Like... labeling camera cards wrong, or just missing a timecode note. Sometimes I'll export a client cut with the wrong lower-third, and the thing is, I'll do that even after I’ve already checked it. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When you're working on a project, are you able to concentrate and focus on the details, or do you find your mind wandering or having trouble keeping your attention on the task?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed my mind wandering, I guess. I just... I do the work, and then I find out later that I messed up those details. So, I don't really know.
Over the past few weeks or months, have you been feeling down, sad, or anxious most of the time? Or has your mood been pretty normal overall?
Um, no... I don't think so. My mood has been fine. Just... normal, I guess. I mean, I get frustrated about the work stuff, but... no, I haven't really felt sad or anything.
Have you had these kinds of careless mistakes and trouble with details for most of your life, or is this something that's relatively new for you?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess... I don't really know if it's new or not. I just know it's causing problems at work right now.
Looking back to when you were in school or early in your career, did you tend to make careless mistakes like this back then, or is this really something that's just started happening recently?

Um... I don't really know about the mistakes specifically. But... I guess things have always been a little difficult. Like, even back in elementary school... my teachers were always moving my desk. Just because I was always getting out of my seat, or... blurting out answers. Bothering the other kids before I even realized I was doing it. So... no, I guess it's not just recently.

Besides work and school, have you noticed these kinds of issues with impulsivity or difficulty sitting still in other parts of your life—like in social situations, at home, or during leisure activities?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed it much outside of work, I guess. I don't really pay attention to how I am at home or... with people. Mostly it's just work where it's a problem. So... I don't know.

You mentioned that back in elementary school you were getting out of your seat and blurting out answers. As you got older—through middle school, high school, and into adulthood—did those kinds of behaviors continue, or did they get better over time?

Um... I don't really remember much about middle school or high school, to be honest. I guess... maybe it just sort of blended in? I don't really know if it got better or... if I just got used to it. I haven't really thought about it.

When you were doing camera work or similar detailed technical tasks earlier in your career—say, in your first few years after school—were you making these kinds of careless mistakes back then, or is this something that's gotten worse recently?

Um... I don't really know. The early years are kind of a blur, to be honest. I just sort of did the work. I haven't really kept track of whether I made mistakes back then or... if it's worse now. I'm not really sure.
Right now at work, are you making these careless mistakes more often than you used to, or have you always tended to make mistakes like this throughout your career?

Um... I guess it's worse now. It hasn't always been this bad. It's been... maybe a little over two years? Like two years and a couple of months. The company had this big readjustment thing, and it changed how all my shoots and edit reviews are scheduled and run. So... yeah, it's been more of a problem since then.

Around the time when your company made that big readjustment about two years ago, did anything else happen in your life—like an illness, an injury, a medication change, or anything like that—that might have coincided with when you started having more trouble with these mistakes?
No, not really. I didn't get sick or anything. It was just... work changing. Nothing else happened.

In the two years since your company made that readjustment, have you had any head injuries, accidents, falls, or any kind of medical problems—like infections, seizures, or anything affecting your brain or nervous system?
Um... no. Nothing like that. I haven't had any accidents or... medical issues. Just normal.

When your company made that big readjustment two years ago, was that a stressful time for you? And did you notice the mistakes starting right around when that happened, or was there a delay of weeks or months before they became a problem?

Um... I guess it was a little stressful. Just... having to get used to the new schedule. And... I don't really remember exactly when the mistakes started. It was just... around then, I think. I didn't really keep track.
Since the company made that readjustment two years ago, have these mistakes at work been getting steadily worse over time, or have they stayed about the same level since they started?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if it's worse. I guess it's probably just... stayed about the same. It's hard to tell.

When the company made that readjustment two years ago, did your work mistakes start happening suddenly right around that time, or had you been making similar careless mistakes at work even before that—just maybe not as noticeably?
I don't really know. I mean... I guess I've always made little mistakes here and there. But I don't think it was this bad before. It's hard to remember.

When your company made that readjustment two years ago, did you notice the mistakes starting to happen within the first week or two after the change happened, or did it take longer—like weeks or months—before you really started noticing the problem?
I... I'm really not sure. I wasn't really keeping track of the timeline. It's just... a blur, honestly. I don't know exactly when it started.
In the past two or three years, have you had any head injuries, concussions, or hits to the head—even minor ones that you might not have thought were serious at the time?
No... no, I haven't. Nothing like that.

Around the time your company made that readjustment two years ago, did you start taking any new medications, or did you have any infections, high fevers, or anything like that happening in your life at that time?
No... I didn't. I wasn't taking anything new. And I don't remember being sick or having a fever or anything like that... so, no.
